Write only the functions asked for. Every run is seeded, so your results are reproducible. The visible tests can be run as often as you like; the hidden tests run when you submit.

questions.title: Metropolis-Hastings for a Bernoulli probability
questions.text:
Binary data $Y_1,\dots,Y_n$ are modelled as conditionally i.i.d. $Y_i\mid p\sim\text{Bernoulli}(p)$, so
$$f(y\mid p)=p^{y}(1-p)^{1-y},\qquad y\in\{0,1\}.$$
The prior on $p$ is a normal distribution with mean $\mu=0.5$ and standard deviation $\sigma=0.2$ **truncated to $(0,1)$**, so that
$$\pi(p)\propto \exp\!\Big(-\frac{(p-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\Big),\qquad 0<p<1.$$

Write two functions.

1. `log_posterior(p, Y)` returns the **unnormalised log posterior** of $p$ given the data array `Y`, and `-np.inf` when $p\notin(0,1)$.
2. `mh_posterior(Y, rng)` runs a **random-walk Metropolis-Hastings** chain for $p\mid Y$ and returns **one numpy array**: the draws left after discarding the burn-in.

The constants `MU`, `SIGMA`, `STEP` (sd of the normal proposal), `P0` (starting value), `N_ITER` (iterations) and `BURN_IN` are already defined for you. The chain makes exactly `N_ITER` iterations, stores the state after every iteration (the current value if the proposal is rejected), and returns the last `N_ITER - BURN_IN` stored values. Use the generator `rng` for all randomness. Only the output of `mh_posterior` is tested, through its 5%, 50% and 95% quantiles.
questions.docs:
**Random-walk Metropolis-Hastings.** Target density $\tilde\pi(p)=f(y\mid p)\,\pi(p)$, known up to a constant.

```
p <- P0
for t = 1, ..., N_ITER:
    p* <- p + STEP * Z,   Z ~ N(0, 1)
    u  <- Uniform(0, 1)
    if log(u) < log pi~(p*) - log pi~(p):
        p <- p*              # accept
    store p                  # also when the proposal was rejected
return the stored values after the first BURN_IN
```

The proposal is symmetric, so the Hastings ratio reduces to $\tilde\pi(p^*)/\tilde\pi(p)$. Work on the log scale to avoid underflow. A proposal outside $(0,1)$ has log posterior $-\infty$ and is always rejected.

For data $y$ with $s=\sum y_i$ the log likelihood is $s\log p+(n-s)\log(1-p)$.

questions.referenceSolution:
def log_posterior(p, Y):
    if p <= 0 or p >= 1:
        return -np.inf
    Y = np.asarray(Y)
    loglik = np.sum(Y * np.log(p) + (1 - Y) * np.log(1 - p))
    logprior = -0.5 * ((p - MU) / SIGMA) ** 2
    return loglik + logprior


def mh_posterior(Y, rng):
    p = P0
    lp = log_posterior(p, Y)
    draws = np.empty(N_ITER)
    for t in range(N_ITER):
        prop = p + STEP * rng.standard_normal()
        lp_prop = log_posterior(prop, Y)
        if np.log(rng.uniform()) < lp_prop - lp:
            p, lp = prop, lp_prop
        draws[t] = p
    return draws[BURN_IN:]
questions.oracleSolution:
def expected_value(Y):
    # independent of MCMC: normalise the posterior on a fine grid and read off the quantiles
    Y = np.asarray(Y)
    s, n = Y.sum(), len(Y)
    p = np.linspace(1e-6, 1 - 1e-6, 400001)
    logpost = s * np.log(p) + (n - s) * np.log1p(-p) - 0.5 * ((p - MU) / SIGMA) ** 2
    w = np.exp(logpost - logpost.max())
    cdf = np.cumsum(w)
    cdf /= cdf[-1]
    return [float(np.interp(q, cdf, p)) for q in (0.05, 0.5, 0.95)]
